records.rationale: The diff explicitly shows `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, ...)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, ...));` — the AND means only users who are BOTH admin AND owner pass, contradicting the permission intent (and the variable name 'AdminOrOwner'). Non-owner team admins are wrongly denied; the team path requires both roles. This is a real logic defect directly verifiable in addGuests.handler.ts.

records.issue_text: Unbounded guests array (no max() on z.array in addGuests.schema.ts) with no rate limiting, combined with attendee authorization path — any authenticated attendee on any booking can create thousands of attendee rows and trigger thousands of invite emails in a single API call (email-bombing vector)
records.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: addGuests.schema.ts defines guests: z.array(z.string().email()) with no length cap, the handler authorizes any attendee (isAttendee path), creates attendees via createMany with uniqueGuests (only filtering duplicates/blacklist), and sends emails to all attendees per call. No rate limiting appears in the diff. Unbounded input combined with email-sending is a plausible abuse/security defect introduced by this code.

records.issue_text: Unused `credentials` include in addGuests.handler.ts over-fetches all credential rows for the booking owner (including encrypted key material) on every call, causing wasted I/O and unnecessary in-memory exposure of credential payloads
records.rationale: The handler's prisma.booking.findFirst includes user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }, yet the only credentials actually used are obtained via the separate getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) call passed to EventManager; booking.user.credentials is never referenced in the handler. So the include does over-fetch credential rows (which contain encrypted key material) for the booking owner on every call.
